title: Local review hard-stops when discovered concerns are not serialized into handoff records

provenance.originSummary: Synthetic benchmark scenario designed to exercise the reviewer-to-handoff completeness gate directly.
provenance.whyItMattered: Use this case to benchmark that the generic local review workflow requires immediate handoff emission during mandatory issue-class checks and still fails closed through coordinator-owned linkage validation before routed roles when a discovered concern is not materialized.
provenance.genericCondition: Sanitized fixture models a review-workflow change where the shared contract owns the immediate-emission rule and the coordinator plus local review prompt are thin consumers that invoke that contract-owned behavior instead of restating it independently.

description: A sanitized local-review scenario where reviewer analysis discovers one blocking concern and one non-blocking concern, but the workflow wording would allow issue-class completion without immediate linkage of those concerns to structured handoff record IDs or would let prompt or coordinator wording drift away from the contract-owned rule. The correct review should flag that as a workflow-breaking gap.

scope.notes: Sanitized fixture models the reviewer-to-handoff serialization gap where mandatory issue-class checks can be marked complete even when no handoff record IDs were emitted immediately for discovered concerns and coordinator-owned linkage validation was not defined as a backstop.

mustCatch.description: The review should raise a real workflow issue if the contract-owned rule can drift across the prompt or coordinator consumers, or if a mandatory issue-class check can find a concern without emitting a matching handoff record ID immediately before continuing the audit and before routed roles begin.

The review should require the coverage matrix to track emitted record IDs and issue-class-to-record-ID bindings so completion can be tied to actual serialized findings at the moment they are discovered instead of reviewer prose or delayed bulk serialization.

mustNotFlag.description: The review must not accept a design that relies on architect, advocate, moderator, or presentation to recover concerns that the reviewer never serialized into the handoff record set.

notes: Use this case to benchmark the contract-owned immediate-emission rule plus the coordinator-owned pre-routing serialization invariant in the generic local review workflow.
